utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. First, a question, does your laptop now function, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see Your Honour that you are the person most familiar with laptops but mine is up to no good. It seems to be breaking down all the time. But apparently it's working for the time being so we'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, although laptops are no fundamental procedural right, at the same time the Chamber was glad to wait for a couple of more minutes to see that it would function at this moment. We are glad that you have it available. Mr. Margetts, are you ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's KRAJ 671 Izet Mehinagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, no protective measures. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Mehinagic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is being brought in just as an addendum to the -- the laptop issue, which is something I think we may need to take up with the Trial Chamber at some point, the -- we've received magnificent assistance from the audio visual department in relation -- to try to ensure that it works, but there is a problem in terms of the computer havening been set up by a different department, and there are password issues and what have you, so it seems to me there may need to be some coordination between them, Your Honour, and it may need the assistance of the Trial Chamber in that regard to ensure ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you fail to establish such a coordination and if the assistance of the registry in this respect would not help out sufficiently, then of course you can address the Chamber and we'll try to assist you as good as we can.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although this Chamber is not composed of whiz kids.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mehinagic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your answer, I understand you hear me in a language you understand. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehinagic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, you will first be examined by Mr. Margetts, counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Margetts, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are utilising the 89(F) procedure with this witness and, as the first exhibit, I would like to introduce the ICTY statement which has been redacted and that is the statement of 25 April 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, if I understand well, the four lines on page 2 have been taken out and the line we discussed yesterday on page 3 have been taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we spent 20 minutes on a matter that could have been solved by the parties, which was a waste of time looking at the result at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have an exhibit number for the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The 89(F) ICTY witness statement dated 25th April, 2003 would be given Prosecution Exhibit P644 and the translation would be P644.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I proceed with the reading of the 89(F) summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may -- I've got one question, however, there's always a problem, what's the original and what's the translation. Could you help us out because otherwise -- is the B/C/S the original or is the English the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The English is the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So 644.1 would be the translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 89(F) summary of the evidence that will be admitted in the exhibit P644 is as follows: When the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina broke out in early 1992, Mr. Mehinagic was a leading member of the Zvornik community. At this time, he was in charge of one of the largest construction projects in the former Yugoslavia, the construction of the Tuzla-Zvornik railroad. He continues to occupy high office today, being council to a federal minister in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In his capacity as general manager for the construction project, Mr. Mehinagic met Momcilo Krajisnik in early 1991. He met with Krajisnik and other high-level members of the Bosnian and Herzegovinian government to promote the project and ensure that adequate funds were allocated to the project. The witness met General Milutin Kukanjac during the 1980s and other prominent members of the JNA including General Savo Jankovic. He maintained frequent contacts with Jankovic through 1991 and early 1992. The witness met Colonel Radoslav Tacic in around January or February of 1992. Tacic was the commander of an armoured brigade. By the end of March 1992, an armoured-mechanised battalion commanded by Dragan Obrenovic and subordinate to Tacic was stationed in Zvornik. From early January 1992, it's Serbs in Zvornik boycotted the Assembly sessions in Zvornik. In meetings with local Serb leaders, they repeatedly stated that Serbs and Muslims could not live together. Mr. Mehinagic considered this idea to be preposterous. Zvornik was a successful business-minded municipality and its success was the result of joint hard work of Serbs and Muslims. On the 8th of April, 1992, Zvornik was attacked. The witness describes meetings he had with local members of the SDA, General Savo Jankovic, and other high-ranking military officials in the week prior to the attack on Zvornik. During the course of the meetings, Mr. Mehinagic discussed means by which peace could be maintained and the people of Zvornik may be defended. When Zvornik was attacked, Mr. Mehinagic sent a telegram to General Savo Jankovic of the JNA pleading with him to protect the endangered population from a catastrophe such as they have never experienced in history. He stated that he sent the dispatch as a cry to heaven and an appeal to act in the line with the most illustrious tradition of the JNA and the most sacred moral norms of our peoples. Prior to the attacks, there had been various meetings between the leaders of the Muslims in Zvornik and the leaders of the Serbs. At a meet are of the Assembly held on 3 April 1992, the session was discontinued after the Serb representatives requested that the municipality be divided into two parts, Serb and Muslim. On 4 April, 1992, the Serbian Territorial Defence of Zvornik was mobilised. On 5 April 1992, Mr. Mehinagic met General Jankovic in the company of Pasic, the president of the municipality, and Jovo Ivanovic, a Serb who was present of the executive council of Zvornik. Ivanovic told Mehinagic and Pasic that there was no use in meeting Jankovic since there was no use in further talks. On the 1st of April 1992 there was an attempt to divide the police in Zvornik between Serbs and Muslims after a dispatch was received from Momcilo Mandic; however, the division of the police did not take place until the 6th of April 1992. On the 6th of April, 1992, barricades were established by the Serb police and Serbian paramilitary forces. On the 6th of April 1992, Mr. Mehinagic attended the first session of the Council of National Defence in Zvornik. The dominant issue raised by the Serbs was division of the municipality into a Serb and Muslim part. Division of the municipality was presented as virtually a non-negotiable fait accomplis. Mr. Mehinagic considered division to be impossible and untenable; however, the Muslim representatives accepted this discussion to buy time. They considered that if they didn't then the Serb representatives would utilise this supposed failure to negotiate as a basis for an attack on the municipality. After this meeting, Mr. Mehinagic participated in the establishment of a Crisis Staff of the Zvornik municipality. On the 7th of April, 1992, a second session of the council of national Defence was held. At this meeting, the JNA commander Tacic stated that the JNA would take over the barricades that had formed in Zvornik and protect people in case of an attack. On the day of the attack, the 8th of April, 1992, the Muslim leaders Pasic and Kapidzic attended a meeting with representatives of the SDS, Jovo Mijatovic and Jovo Ivanovic. The paramilitary leader Arkan entered this meeting, slapped the SDS representatives and told them that the SDS representatives had nothing to negotiate with the other side and the only competent body to decide the fate of Zvornik was the Assembly. Arkan stated that unless the Muslims laid down their weapons by 1700, the destiny of Zvornik would be the same as Bijeljina. Mehinagic contacted General Savo Jankovic to ask him to put the tanks in a defensive position however Jankovic responded by simply asking him whether his family was in a safe place. Mehinagic immediately wrote the dispatch that I've already referred to, to Jankovic, sending the dispatch as a cry to heaven to the JNA forces to save the people of Zvornik. When Mehinagic wrote this telegram, the shelling of Zvornik had already commenced and shells were being fired from JNA positions. Mehinagic immediately left Zvornik after writing the telegram and fled to Tuzla with his family. In Tuzla, Mr. Mehinagic established the organisation that was to become the association for Zvornik refugees in Tuzla. On the 8th of May 1992, he established the Zvornik municipality in exile. Mr. Mehinagic sent the declaration of the Zvornik municipality to the Territorial Defence office in Zvornik and he was contacted by the Territorial Defence commander Marko Pavlovic who accused him of inciting people to rebellion and threatened him. Mr. Mehinagic also established the municipal commission for the investigation of war crimes. The commission received information from people who were refugees and had fled to Tuzla. Mr. Mehinagic made efforts to publicise crimes that he was informed were taking place in Zvornik. From the 17th of June, 1992 up to October 1992, Mr. Mehinagic was deputy of the coordinating council of the region of Tuzla. This body dealt with all civilian problems and coordinated the regional Territorial Defence Staff. That concludes the summary. Your Honour, if I may proceed with the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, do you have a copy before you of your ICTY statement in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I do, Mr. Margetts; I got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could refer to paragraphs 3 to 6 of the statement, in these paragraphs you refer to your role as general manager of the public construction company for railway tracks from Tuzla to Zvornik and you described that in this role you regularly reported to the prime minister Jure Pelivan and the minister of finance; further, you were required to meet with senior politicians in Bosnia and Herzegovina including Momcilo Krajisnik in order to ensure adequate funds were allocated to the railway. In regard to these matters, was it important for you to gain the support from the speaker of the Assembly, Momcilo Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I considered it very significant when it came to a project which was one of the most significant ones in the former Yugoslavia to inform the public and the leadership of the country on a regular basis, so I myself thought it was very important that I should report on a regular basis to the speaker of the Assembly and the head of government and so that's why I did it. I met with Mr. Krajisnik twice in this respect and both meetings were successful business meetings and they did not touch upon any political issues except a good realisation and implementation of this project. Mr. Krajisnik gave his support to this project and especially when I met with him in his office at the General Assembly and also on the 5th of December, 1991, when he was heading a high-level republic -- delegation of the republic when he came to the Krizevic tunnel when we had a break through there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I notice that your speed of speech is rather high and I hear that the interpreters have some difficulties in keeping up with you so if you could slow down a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this respect, and this is with respect to paragraph 6, I was in regular contact with the president of the government, Mr. Jure Pelivan, and in one meeting in the course of the month of August 1991, I took the opportunity to make a comment and object to the fact that the leadership of Bosnian Muslims and Croats had asked for them -- for their fellow nationals to leave the JNA because I thought that it was a bad thing for the overall political situation. I thought it was the only legal political power, and so I was horrified by that. But Mr. Pelivan was not a politician, he was a banker. He never counted with any valid arguments he simply waved my comments away and he said it was okay, and he did not at all understand what I was saying. But afterwards, there was a meeting of the Corps commanders at this meeting with the leadership of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could just explain to you the process that we're engaging in here in regards to your evidence. The -- all of the material that you see in the statement before you that does not have a line struck through it is admitted into evidence in writing so it's not necessary for us to cover all those matters orally in the court. In particular, the issue of your meeting with Mr. Jure Pelivan is fully detailed in the evidence that's admitted in writing. So I'm just going to ask you a few questions that help to clarify matters that are in the statement and seek explanations that you can provide the Trial Chamber. So I will just return to the matter of it being important for you to gain the support of Mr. Krajisnik. Why was it important specifically for support to be provided by Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: By virtue of his position, Mr. Krajisnik was after the president of the republic, the second-ranking figure in the leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In view of his position, I thought it important to regularly inform him thereof and, secondly, he played an important role in the adoption of a budget for the construction of the a railway because such a project was always tabled before the Assembly that decided upon it, and Mr. Krajisnik was speaker ever that Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehinagic. Your Honours, if I could present to Mr. Mehinagic the second exhibit which is a telegram dated 8 April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, is this a telegram that you sent to General Savo Jankovic on the 8th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, if I can refer you to the top of the telegram, there's a note that states, "Colleague, please pass this -- pass on this telegram urgently, as urgently as possible as thousands of lives are at stake." Then there's some handwriting there. Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Whose handwriting is that?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you. I see it says here "Inform General Jankovic about the -- what the citizens in Zvornik think." This could be General Kukanjac's handwriting or that of some of his associates because I see that it says Milutin Kukanjac here and General Kukanjac and I were very good friends, we knew each other very well and upon receipt of such a telegram, he had to react in some way, definitely. That was his level of appreciation for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I refer you to the first paragraph of the telegram and in that paragraph, you refer to negotiations attended by Dragan Obrenovic, Alija, who I assume is Alija Kapidzic from the Territorial Staff in Zvornik, and Abdulah, who I assume is Abdulah Pasic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And you state that Arkan was the chief negotiator on behalf of the other side and two representatives were beaten before that. How did you find out about this meeting with Arkan?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: The attack on Zvornik started in the morning at around 8.00 on the 8th of April and the president of the Municipal Assembly of Zvornik sought contacts with the SDS. He managed to achieve negotiations to be scheduled in Zvornik at noon. He was accompanied by the commander, the legal commander of the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Zvornik, Mr. Alija Kapidzic. They were there from 11.00 in the 3.00 p.m. We had no information whatsoever from them and all the while, Zvornik was under attack. At 3.00 p.m., I was in the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence and there was another very good friend of mine there and nobody else but, in fact, the Territorial Defence did not exist at all because it was not supposed to be mobilised under General Kadijevic's order. At that point, Mr. Abdulah Pasic from the centre -- from the crisis centre of the municipality at the Zvornik MUP found me to tell me what had in fact happened in Mali Zvornik. He told me that they had negotiated with Jovo Mijatovic and Jovo Jovanovic who introduced themselves as the president of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik and the president of the executive board, respectively, that it was in this capacity that they negotiated with them. But there was Captain Obrenovic there, and I was even surprised to hear that the then-president of the Municipal Assembly was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It's difficult for the transcriber to keep up with the speed of your speech. It's unusual here because we have simultaneous translation and also the transcription of the material so you'll probably note that I'm speaking inordinately slowly but if I can invite you to slow down just a little bit. But to continue your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best. They said that they were acting under the threat of force. When they saw that at one point Arkan barged into the room and said, "What sort of negotiations are you carrying -- are you conducting here because you have no authorisation to do that for the Serb part." And it was under such pressure that they signed a document on the division of Zvornik contrary to their beliefs and contrary to the conclusions of the council that was attended by all those responsible in Zvornik including the representatives of the Muslims and the Serbs. So it was contrary to these positions and under coercion that they signed this document on the division. He further told me that Arkan, after having slapped these two Serb representatives, also slapped the commander of the TO Zvornik. He said, "Either you will surrender arms by 5.00 p.m. or you will share the destiny of those from Bijeljina." He returned then to Zvornik, phoned me, and we were to agree on what to do next. He said that he had called a meeting of the Crisis Staff of Zvornik for 4.00 p.m. but that since this was an attack on Zvornik that, hadn't been uncalled for and not provoked in any way, and since the fact that the people were defending themselves was the only chance of their survival, he concluded that the Crisis Staff was not going to accept those terms and that what was to ensue was the massacre of the people in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Only now the translation finished. Could I ask you to look at your screen and keep an eye on it, that as long as the text is moving, that is as long as the translation and the transcript is made, that you make a pause and that you restart once it has stopped moving.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, two points of clarification. The first one you said is this, said the head of the TO in Zvornik was also slapped, was that Alija Kapidzic?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The second matter is this, you said that Arkan had told the Serb representatives that they were not -- not authorised to negotiate. Did he indicate where the authority to negotiate would come from?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: According to what President Pasic told me over the phone he had said that testifies only the Assembly that was authorised to do so. Now, as for the meaning of this you would have to ask Arkan. I don't know what he had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'll just read into the record the next part of this telegram and I'll ask for your comment on it. You mention that an ultimatum has been given for the laying down of weapons and then you say the following: Addressing General Savo Jankovic, you say, "I do not think that the ultimatum will be accepted and that this will lead to an unprecedented massacre of the unprotected and innocent population and to horrible environmental consequences as a result of suicidal action by the desperate population. I send you this dispatch as a cry to heaven and an appeal to you to act in line with the most illustrious traditions of the JNA and the most say credit moral norms of our peoples and to protect the endangered population from a catastrophe such as they have never experienced in their history. Your name will go down in history either as the name of a savior or a man who missed the opportunity to become one. The only solution is to deploy your units from the zone in which they now find themselves together with the forces threatening the population and station them at the approaches to the town where they will defend the endangered population from the oppressors." Were the JNA forces redeployed and did they defend the population of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I was very much a legalist and in favour of the JNA forces being deployed in and around Zvornik. At the meeting with General Jankovic that I had organised on the 5th of April, and at another meeting of the Council for National Defence held on the 7th of April, it was jointly concluded and the JNA representatives agreed that they would defend the town if attacked. At that point, that is when I was writing this telegram, I was aware of the fact and certain of the fact that Zvornik came under attack from the area where the JNA had been deployed including, of course, Serbia and I could observe that. However, I wanted to leave open the possibility for the JNA to defend the population whose defence it was responsible for. It was only when he asked me whether I had sent my family away somewhere safe, I told him, "Does this mean that there's nothing further that the two of us have to discuss?" That's when I understood that we were going to be under attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, approximately 12 lines back, I read the question which was: "Were the JNA forces redeployed and did they defend the population of Zvornik?" Until now, you've given us a lot of information but you've not yet answered the question. Would you please focus very much on answering the question and if we'd like, or if Mr. Margetts would like to know more about the background or further details, he'll certainly ask you. We are under some time restraint which for you as a -- in your own capacity, must be a well-known matter. So may I ask you to focus on the question and to start answering that first. So the question was whether the JNA forces were redeployed and whether they defended the population of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to that, Your Honour, if I might just add, it seems to me that the most useful approach may be to actually ask the witness what he saw or heard or what have you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas, I put a question to the witness. Let's first see whether we can get him on track, to focus on the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please answer the question put to you whether the JNA was redeployed and whether they protected the Zvornik population.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The JNA forces were deployed around Zvornik and did not defend the town. They were basically arranged so as to execute an attack on Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mehinagic, I understand fully that the full background and the context was contained in your answer, the full background to the matter that I was dealing with in my question but I just wanted to reassure you again that in order to save time in the court, we actually have all of that information in writing in the -- in evidence and so it's not necessary for us to restate that or reiterate it in the court. I'll just be asking specific questions to develop and clarify those matters that are already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the next exhibit could be presented to Mr. Mehinagic, and that's a transcript of an interview from Tuzla Radio. And, Your Honour, if I may, can we clarify the exhibit number that was given to the telegram of 8 April 1992 if one was already given, or could we have an exhibit number for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it had not been given yet and Mr. Registrar, would that be P645 for the original and P645.1 for the translation?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number has been assigned. And for our next document which is the transcript of an interview, Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next exhibit number would be P646 for the interview, and the translation would be 646.1 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it the interview was taken in B/C/S, Mr. Margetts?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then English would be the translation so the B/C/S original is P646 and the English translation is P646.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, before you is a transcript of an interview that you gave Radio Zvornik -- sorry, Radio Tuzla. Since you've arrived in The Hague, have you had an opportunity to review this transcript?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I've listened. I've reviewed the transcript and listened to the interview in its original form.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And are matters set out here accurate?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if you could just inform the Court, after you sent the telegram to General Jankovic, did you leave Zvornik and, if so, where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: After having sent a telegram to General Jankovic, I put my family into my car and left Zvornik along the Zvornik-Didic-Sultanovic road. On the section of the Zvornik-Didic road, there was heavy gun and artillery fire from the direction of Serbia which targeted the road and the area in general. I told my family to lie down on the floor in the car and I kept driving despite the odds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And you reached Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I spent the night at Glumina at some of my friends house and that's where I could -- from there, I could watch the artillery fire, the shelling of Zvornik. The following morning at 8.30, after having arranged so with Selim Beslagic, the president of the municipal Assembly, and Mesa Bajric, the chief of the SUP who had sent police escort to meet me, I returned -- I went with my family to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could refer you to your statement and if I could refer you to the paragraphs which are 69 to 71. Now, in paragraph 69 to 71, you set out -- you refer to a press conference you gave in Tuzla and a radio interview. Can you confirm to the Court that the transcript that you have before you is a transcript of the interview that's referred to in those paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the transcript of my interview for Radio Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehinagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could refer to the next exhibit which is a videotape of events in Zvornik. The CD will be provided later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The number would be, Mr. Registrar, do we have the -- we look at the videotape, yes. The number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was wondering what this had to do with this part of your examination.

utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, what I'd like to do is move to -- if the exhibit number could be maintained for that video and we will present that at a later time today after we've had time to rectify the problem and if the next exhibit could be the next one in order, which is the transcript of interview with Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will be providing the CD. If I could turn Your Honour to page 13 of the English translation for both Your Honours and Mr. Mehinagic's benefit, that is the sequence that starts at the timing reference, 1:29:39, and if that first clip could be played.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "And quite by coincidence, I set off with my aide-de-camp. We sent off for Mali Zvornik because they had called us urgently to go over there and when I arrived I went straight over to a meeting. The meeting was attended by the commander of the SDA Zvornik, the commander of the Zvornik Crisis Staff, a Turk, and on the other side, the commander of the SDS Crisis Staff and president of the Zvornik SDS. At Mali Zvornik on the other side of the Drina river, when asked about what they were talk being they said, "You know, the Muslims have taken over Zvornik and we're insisting that they let the Serbs go and we will hand Karakaj over to them." That was the story. Which is another part of Zvornik. "Naturally, I asked those two Serbs who authorised you to discuss -- to negotiate for treason. No one has the authority to negotiate for treason and naturally I caught them and beat both of them up, both one and the other. They were slapped a couple of times. We didn't touch the Turks. I just gave them a pencil and a piece of paper to write down how many weapons they had. And when they saw us beating up Serbs, they wondered what we would do to them. And they wrote down the number of 700 armed men on a piece of paper, where their units were, how they were deployed, who was leading them and so forth. "Then I asked them, "Did you here to negotiate?" They said "Yes, we did." I gave them an ultimatum to surrender the town by 0800 hours; otherwise, I would destroy it. That's how it was. At 0500 hours, they did not want to surrender the town. I ordered artillery fire and naturally we entered Zvornik at 0500 hours. Fighting went on throughout the day. Zvornik was seized. We had a lot of prisoners. There were many dead on their side because they were not skilled in combat. They died in sheaves. They died in sheaves. They were fanatics. So there was fierce fighting which last the several hours and we came out as the winners. "Kula was still theirs. They resisted over there and two of my security officers were killed as a result of naivete. A group of Muslims was surrendering, about 40 of them, while snipers waited on the other side. And then when two of them came out of the shelter to meet those who were surrendering, the snipers killed them from the side. "And naturally, we continued fighting until we captured ... with the help of others, we captured Kula, and so forth. Later, we left Zvornik after a couple of days and they established a government over there which did not function at first, because a lot of trash came over from Serbia who even looted and stole from the Serbs. "I returned once to Zvornik after spending a several days in Erdut and I had to impose discipline to slap the authorities around; they were actually a band of rabble. And, you know, later, special police units came from Pale and disarmed all those people who were in Zvornik and arrested them. "And what happened afterwards with your unit?" Arkan: "Well after that, our unit ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, I'd just like to ask you a question about that interview with Arkan. He stated at the beginning that he had obtained information that the Muslims had taken over Zvornik on the 8th of April, 1992; was that the case?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: On the night between the 5th and the 6th of April 1992, under the circumstances that I've described in great detail in my statement, Serbs --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Can I just stop you there. We've only got a short time for the examination so I'm going to ask you some very specific questions and if you can just address yourself to the question and once again, be assured that all of the background is dealt with in detail in the statement that's admitted into evidence. So I'll just ask you that question again, and that is: Had the Muslims taken over Zvornik when Arkan arrived in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next question is this: He said here that he asked the Serb authorities who authorised them to discuss treason and he said that no one has a mandate to discuss treason. You've detailed to the Court what Mr. Pasic told you after your -- after this meeting. Is that consistent with what Mr. Pasic told you occurred and what Mr. Arkan said?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to that, Your Honours, that sort of question is actually of no assistance to the Trial Chamber. Your Honours have heard the evidence, you have the evidence before you in the statement as well as to the information that was conveyed to Mr. Pasic. Consistency or otherwise is of course a matter for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's -- whether the witness sees any inconsistency might be of assistance to the Chamber. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, do you see that as being the same message that Mr. Pasic gave you as to what Mr. Arkan said?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I do recognise what I was told by Mr. Pasic on the phone here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next matter is that Arkan says that there was fighting and that they -- the Serbs had a lot of prisoners and there were many dead on the other side and that they died in sheaves. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Obviously I can't testify about that because I was no longer at Zvornik. According to my information, that could have been civilians but I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: When you went to Tuzla, did any person who was present in Zvornik inform you as to what had happened after you you'd left on the 8th and 9th of April?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Of course I was getting reports, the President Pasic still had some kind of moral obligation to me so he did report to me on occasion when we met about those events. Also refugees would tell me about everything and victims as well who used to come from that area and afterwards, all the structures of the municipality of Tuzla had been set up so I had all the reports that went through the structure. And that's the basis for the information I got.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And what information did you receive about deaths on the -- at the time that Arkan's units and other forces took over Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: According to that information, basically Zvornik was left on the 9th of April and the defenders with a couple of thousands of the local inhabitants, the local population, they took shelter in Kula and according to the news from TV Belgrade, there were about 74 people killed so it could be ascribed to the overall number of civilians killed. But there were quite a few video and TV reports referring to all that. According to my information and on the basis of all the information I got at that stage, and during the following month between 300 and 500 people had been killed in the city of Zvornik itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Arkan, toward of the end of that clip that we showed you, says that he had to return to Zvornik and slap the authorities around. After you left Zvornik, did you receive information as to which authorities obtained power in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: My information confirmed what Arkan has said because there was an overall state of confusion, there was looting and rapes also aimed at Serb women and girls and they were victims of those Serb formations as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Once yourself and Mr. Pasic left Zvornik, did you receive any information as to who became president of the municipality or led the municipality of Zvornik in the city of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: We would get that information from the refugees and we also listened to the so-called Serb Radio Zvornik so we got some information that way as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What was that information as regards who became the president of the municipality and which organised authority was in control of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: According to that information, initially, Jovo Mijatovic and Jovo Jovanovic respectively. And then there was some sort of interim government presided over by Brano Grujic and thereupon, in 1992, the -- there was Brano Grujic and then for the executive committee, it was a professor called Radoslav Peric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In regard to Grujic, Mijatovic and Ivanovic, which political party were they affiliated with?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: They were all members of the Serb Democratic Party and Grujic was the president of one of the SDS committee and Mijatovic was a member of the republic Assembly. And Ivanovic, as one of the leaders of the SDS was the president of the municipal committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to play another clip from the exhibit P648 and that is a clip that begins at the counter reference 1:23:13 which is beginning at the bottom of page 10 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This is the war. Now we've come to the war in the Republika Srpska. You had -- you had your activities going on. We had some data according to which Muslims had gotten organised. Some members of our own Serb guard coming from the area we were reporting to us on a regular basis and Vojkan Curkovic, he now works on exchanges and he supplied us with regular information about the situation in Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed -- I noticed, Mr. Margetts, that compared to the transcripts, that parts of the translations were missing, especially on the -- where it goes from page 10 to 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if we may play that clip again and I'll just orient the translators again to the counter reference, it's 1:23:13.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Yes, it was here at Celic. That's already the war in Republika Srpska. So we have come to the war in Republika Srpska. You already had the halo of a warrior and soldier. You commenced your operations in Bijeljina. Yes. So we at the invitation of the Serb Democratic Party because they already knew here we had information that the Muslims had organised themselves. Even some members of our Serbian volunteer guard who are from here gave us regular information. Vojkan Curkovic he now works in exchanges and they supplied us with regular information about the situation in Republika Srpska, I think, then Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, Arkan states in this interview that in response to a question about commencing his operations in Bijeljina, that he was at the invitation of the Serbian Democratic Party. Do you have any information that you can give to the Trial Chamber in regard to Mr. Arkan's association or otherwise with the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I really can't testify properly about this other than the points I've already made, that is to say the fact that he was present in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And you stated earlier that the leaders of the Zvornik municipality after Arkan's forces were engaged were the members of the SDS. Is that correct, did the SDS assume control of the municipal organs after the attack on Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that question. The witness has quite clearly stated that his information in relation to the leadership becomes second or third hand and the question has already been asked in relation to this issue and, Your Honours, I object to this further attempt by the Prosecutor in relation to the same area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm quite happy to withdraw that question and move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: So I do formally withdraw that prior -- previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mehinagic, I'd like to move on from that exhibit and I'd like to present a bunch of exhibits to the witness and these are the documents that appear on the exhibit list between numbers 7 and 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note that the first two documents, and they are documents 7 and 8, already have exhibit numbers but if the documents 9, 10, and 11 could each be provided individual exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have not seen yet Exhibit 6 on your list, Mr. Margetts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct due to the malfunction of the video, I haven't been able to move to that exhibit. But I intend to come back to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then for -- Mr. Registrar, first of all, for exhibit on the list number 9, which is an announcement of the first regular session of the Assembly of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P649, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And then the next one, the decision on the proclamation of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be 650, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the decision on the association of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik to the region of Majevica, Semberija, and Birac.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be 651, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, during the period late 1991 and early 1992, were you in regular contact with Mr. Pasic and other leaders of the Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: In the capacity of the manager of the railway, I was in regular contacts with municipal leaders. Since my job was a very demanding one -- these were of course business contacts and meetings at some crucial points of the realisation of the project. On the eve of the events that I'm testifying about, a month earlier, I realised that something important was happening and that I, as a person with a public profile, had to do something.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mehinagic, I again I reiterate that your activities during that period are detailed in your statement. I just want to refer you to the first document that was presented to you, it's a document dated at the top 22nd December 1991, and it sets out the conclusions of the Zvornik Municipal Board meeting held on the 22nd of December 1991. You'll see at point 3 that a Crisis Staff has been elected and you'll see at point 6 that the Assembly of the Serb People of the municipality of Zvornik in scheduled for the 27th of December 1991. Were you aware at that time either that a Crisis Staff had been formed by the SDS or that a Serb Assembly was to meet in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I can take you to the second document and that's the document headed decision regarding the formation of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik. And that decision refers to Assembly session held on the 27th of December, 1991 and in article 2 of that decision, there is the definition of the region of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik and to the areas that that includes. Could you just cast your eye over those areas described there. Now, at that time, were you aware that there had been a decision on the formation of the Serbian municipality and this Serbian municipality was to be constituted by those areas described there?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I did not know. This is the first time that I saw the document here, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What is your response to Article 2 of this decision, that is, to an Assembly of the Serbian People of Zvornik being the Assembly responsible for the regions defined there?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would object to the formulation of the question. "What is your response to Article 2," I would submit, is not a focused question, and may lead to an unfocussed answer. I think if Mr. Margetts is seeking a response in relation to this issue, to ask "What is your response," without focussing question will lead to an unfocussed answer in my submission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if he focuses on specific matters then he risks of finding it objected by being leading. Mr. Margetts, of course, if the answer is vague but it's a very open question but it can be put to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, just restating the question, looking at Article 2 there where there is a reference to regions and I'll actually just repeat the question, and the question was this: What is your response to Article 2 of this decision, that is, to an Assembly of the Serbian People of Zvornik being the Assembly responsible for the regions defined in Article 2?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: My attitude then and my attitude now has been and still is that it is impossible, unacceptable, and irrational; and, secondly, there was always a Serb Knez, or a Serb chief in a Serb village, and the Muslim villages were headed by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, I'll refer you to the next document and that is a document dated 11 March, 1992 and it's a notice to all deputies of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik and it states that the first regular session of the Assembly of the Serbian municipality will be held on the 15th of March, 1992. Were you aware that such a meeting was scheduled for the 15th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I didn't know, and as I've said, I've only seen this document here and then I find out that this was convened, this meeting was convened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And I'd like to refer you to the next document which is dated 15 March, 1992 and is a decision on the proclamation of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik and I'd in particular like to direct your attention to the definition of the territory of the Serbian municipality and the territory is defined by reference to the decision we previously saw. That is, the territory is defined pursuant to Article 2 of the decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik. Were you aware that on the 15th of March, 1992, the Serbian municipality of Zvornik was proclaimed and it was to include the territories we looked at a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? Are you referring to the Serb municipality of Zvornik or the region of Birac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I think we may have -- my next question relates to the document addressing the regional matters. This question is directed to a document dated 15 March 1992 headed, "Decision on the proclamation of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik." Do you have that decision before you?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: So my question was on the 15th of March, 1992, were you aware that the municipality of Zvornik had been proclaimed and were you aware that that Serbian municipality consisted of the territories that we saw described in the earlier decision dated 27 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'll now move to the final document from this series and this is a decision on the association of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik to the regions of Majevica Semberija and Birac. Again this decision is dated 15 March 1992. Did you have any information in relation to the formation of the Serbian regions of Birac?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Exactly at that time, I was watching television and there was a report from the founding Assembly for this region of Birac and it was held at Sekovici. I remember that because in the first row, I saw a good friend of mine, Bozo Milic, who was their president of the executive committee for Vlasenica. And I thought that he was out of place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What nationality or what ethnicity was Mr. Milic?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if those documents could be returned, and the next exhibit could be presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could I ask, we are close to 10.30, Mr. Margetts, I don't know whether you could deal with the next one. I would have one question in relation to one of these exhibits. And that's the document of the 22nd of December, 1991, which is already in evidence as P529 tab 40. Mr. Mehinagic, I do understand that you only became later aware of the existence of a Serbian or SDS Crisis Staff. In this document which says that a Crisis Staff for the municipality of Zvornik is elected, I first of all see quite some names but there's one position which is not mentioned by name but by function, that is Command Staff of Zvornik municipality. Do you know who was to be considered command staff of Zvornik municipality in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously I'm seeing this document for the first time and I find it rather surprising because I did not know that there was a command staff of JNA in the municipality of Zvornik. It could have been Major Zoran Jovanovic by the nature of things, he was a good friend of mine. He used to work at the factory in Birac or Obrenovic who was the commander of the armoured battalion of the JNA. But he was not there at the time, he had not arrived yet, so he couldn't have been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You, in your statement, you have given a lot of observations in respect of the JNA just prior to and during the attack at -- on Zvornik. The information that the command staff of Zvornik municipality JNA was elected as a member or at least an organisation which was part of the Crisis Staff, does that give you any reason to adjust or to complete the observations you have made about the role of the JNA during the attack on Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be honest, considering my relationship with the JNA commanders, I'm wondering whether it was JNA staff for Zvornik at all. And in case it was, it may have been established on the other side of Drina because I'm convinced that General Jankovic would have informed me of the existence of some sort of staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was there -- you've repeatedly said that you look at matters also from the formal point of view. From a formal point of view, could any JNA command commit itself to a municipal Crisis Staff formed by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In legal terms, no, never. From a purely legal point of view, because they should be separate from any political party, according to what is enshrined in law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just have one further question and that is the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In your statement, you observed that the SDS members of the Zvornik Assembly, that's the mixed nationality Assembly, had ceased attending meetings of the Zvornik Assembly. Having seen these documents, do they assist you in understanding the -- understanding the events you have observed in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Glancing at these documents, I realise why the councillors from the General Assembly of Zvornik boycotted the Assembly meetings. Between the end of December and the 3rd of April when a meeting was held. The reason, obviously, was the setting up of some kind of Serb municipality on the 27th of December, some sort of illegal Serb municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehinagic. That would be an appropriate time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. Margetts. Mr. Mehinagic, we will have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could now return to the video that we unsuccessfully attempted to play earlier and that's P647 and if we could play that. And Mr. Mehinagic, if you could watch the screen in front of you, we're going to play the video we attempted to play earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] I could say that there isn't any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. particular reason ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, only now the English translation appears on the transcript so we have to restart and see whether we get everything, every spoken single word.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the purposes of the examination of this witness, if we could just play the video, and we could not have a simultaneous translation into English. There are some subtitles which will appear on the video and I don't think that will in any way affect the comments that I'm seeking from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, would you agree with such a procedure, that is, that Mr. Margetts takes the view that the text spoken is not of any relevance for what he wants to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if -- yes, the text spoken is not of any relevance, then it's merely for the playing of the video, then I don't take any objection to that cause. If there were to be any questions to relation to the text then quite clearly we would need a proper translation in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then the parties agree on it. This could have been better announced from the beginning, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We were a bit surprised by this different approach from the usual approach. Could we restart?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, and just a direction to the translators that there's no need for them to translate the spoken word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, was the footage shown of the soldiers and the other various scenes depicted footage of the city of Zvornik and its surrounds?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, I'd like to show you some still clips and the first one appears at 17 minutes 18 seconds on the video. Can you identify this man?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This is Brano Grujic, president of the Municipal SDS Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The second one I'd like to show you appears at 17 minutes 42.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This is Adbulah Pasic, president of the Zvornik Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The third one I'd like to show you appears at 19 minutes 58.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Mendiluce who spoke of what he had experienced in Zvornik. I met him in Sarajevo when he was promoting his book on his experience in Bosnia. And he told me the very same thing he stated in this footage. What you can hear -- what you can see here is some members of the defence, the man holding a rifle is Fajdo from the area of Bukovik that was first under attack and he returned to his home. He lives in Zvornik today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: This still is 19 minutes 47 on the tape. After this attack, where did this gentleman go, did he remain in Zvornik or did he leave?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: He fled to Tuzla where I used to meet him occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: This is at the tape, 20 minutes and 10 seconds. Do you recognise that man?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This is Esad Srabovic, an engineer from the Glinica factory in Birac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Did he remain in Zvornik or did he leave?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: No, he fled to Tuzla and then from there, he went abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next one is from 20 minutes and 30 seconds. Do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This is an eminent economician, Talic, from the same Glinica factory; he currently resides in the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Did you know when he left Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This took place in early April when the exodus from Zvornik was organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Esad Srabovic and Mr. Taljic, what ethnicity from they?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: They were Muslims, Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, that's not the correct still. I'll move to the next one. This is at 21 minutes 43. Can you identify that man who is being held by the soldier?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This is Muhamed Zaimovic, the erstwhile president of the municipal court of Zvornik. He was detained in Zvornik for a while and then he fled abroad. Today he lives at Vogosca near Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And the next clip which is 22 minutes 56. Can you identify anyone in this clip?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This is the body of Izet Sabirovic a veterinarian, one of the most distinguished figures of Zvornik. He was of course a civilian. He is in this particular clip being taken out of his courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And again would Mr. Muhamed Zaimovic and Mr. Izmet Sabirovic, what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: They were also Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one addition until question in relation to the last clip. Mr. Mehinagic, on the basis of what, exactly, did you identify the deceased person, because it's difficult to see his face. Is it mainly on the environment - as you said, he is taken out from his courtyard - that you concluded that this must be the person you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: First of all, this takes place in his courtyard. Secondly, I viewed this footage with his wife and she confirmed this to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say that on the basis of what his wife told you, which you find supported by what you see as far as the place is concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This was confirmed by numerous other eyewitnesses. They all commented on this particular event and confirmed that that was him. Nobody thought to the contrary, and he was a very distinguished person in the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting in any way that it's not him, but it's important for this Court to know exactly on the basis of what knowledge and on the basis of whose observations we conclude about the identity of this person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I fully understand the position of the Trial Chamber. Since I knew Izet Sabirovic and since what I saw here confirms what I had been -- what I had heard as description, that's why I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could -- I'll continue with the stills but at this point, with this particular still on the display, if I could present the next document to Mr. Mehinagic, and that is the document which appears as number 6 in the witness list, and if that could be given a number. That's the "Order on the Establishment for the Commission of Clearing up a Battlefield."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dated the 19th of May 1992. Mr. Registrar, would that be P652 for the original and P652.1 for the English translation?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, can you look at the names in this document, which is the "order on the establishment for clearing up the battlefield," dated 19 May, 1992 and you'll see that the first name listed in item one is Kosta Eric. Do you know who Costa Eric is?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the time of these events, he was the secretary of the municipal staff of civilian protection. He worked for the municipal staff for national defence. He still lives in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The second name that appears is Nedjo Mladjenovic, can you tell the Court what he is?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Nedjo Mladjenovic is a very good friend of mine, we still on very good terms. At that time, he was the manager of a public utility company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Whilst you were in Tuzla, were you told anything about Mr. Mladjenovic's activities in April and May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I heard from refugees who came from over there that there was this clearing up of a battlefield and on the basis of the report that I received, I heard that the commission had been established quite -- at a quite later stage in relation to the time when the civilians were actually killed. This order that I see now for the first time confirms what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What did you specifically hear about Mr. Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: As manager of a public utility company, he organised trucks and the machinery for digging up mass graves and that he was involved in the burial of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If we could -- I've finished with that exhibit, Mr. Mehinagic. If we could now continue with the stills.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, could we ask about the ethnicity of the president and the members of the commission for clearing up a battlefield. Could you tell us what their ethnicity is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Kosta Eric and Nedjo Mladjenovic are Serbs. I can say that because I know them. As for the other two, I could say the same judging by their names, but I am -- I do not know this for a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My next question to be you told us that Nedjo Mladjenovic is still a good friend of yours. Could you explain to us whether this is your general attitude, that whatever has happened, it does not disturb your friendships or that it was particular behaviour, because we have heard a lot of testimonies where people were very much disappointed in what they thought to be friends. Could you tell us a bit more about a good friend of yours who took up with this function and you still describe him as a good friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have known Nedjo Mladjenovic for a long time because I used to work in the same company he worked for. I was able to see for myself that he was a good man and a good friend. He had to carry out this task as manager of the public utility company and I don't see anything dishonourable in that. And it's on that basis that I still consider him and I still socialise with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you're telling us is that just being a Serb is not to blame anyone for what happened; is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, you've understood me well. I was never of that opinion and I did not change my opinion after the events in 1992 and 1995 and I don't think I will change my view now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts. No, Judge Hanoteau has a question as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bearing this in mind, do you have the statement before you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. Mehinagic has his statement there before him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 5 of the statement, in the English version, paragraph 29, which is quite a lengthy one, much is said about a meeting in which Serb leaders --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe it's paragraph 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [In English] I'm sorry, it's 19. Excuse me. [Interpretation] A meeting where Serb leaders were repeating or saying that Serbs and Muslims could not live together and in your statement, you state that, [In English] ..."could not successfully live together in Zvornik was completely preposterous. One could hardly find the single ethic [sic] members's family." [Interpretation] Could you perhaps clarify this for us? You emphasised the fact that people were working alongside with each other in companies, and you said the industrial and commercial success of the town of Zvornik was due to the joint efforts of a multi-ethnic community. Could you spell this out for us, please, and how can you explain to us the reasons why this came to an end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've stated my attitude very explicitly before, so I'm going to try and keep my answer brief. Zvornik was a municipality with 59 per cent of Bosniaks, 38 per cent Serbs and 2.7 per cent of others. It can be considered that all the way up to the elections where the national parties won in 1990, we enjoyed a harmonious interethnic relationship. We respected one another. We socialised. We were friends. In my own family, my eldest brother is married to a Serb and they're still together. And it was very unusual to find a family, either an extended family or whatever with no such examples. On the other hand, it was a very successful business community and it embraced the project of reform put forward by the former Yugoslav Premier, Ante Markovic, and the results were outstanding. Obviously Serbs and Muslims worked in it together and there were directors and managers and bosses from both groups and there was no national tension in any of these companies. Thirdly, Zvornik is situated at the border with Serbia and we had excellent neighbourly and business relations with Serbia. Most companies from Zvornik enjoyed great cooperation with companies on other side of the border in Serbia. Tens of thousands of people who were employed in Serbia originally came from the area of the municipality of Zvornik and at the Birac factory, for example, Glinica-Birac factory, they were many people what came from Loznica, many employees, I mean, so we really relied on one another and that was the basis for holding a rational view that we can live together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one clarification. In your daily life, there were no clashes between the two communities, between people belonging to different ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Generally speaking, no, not in Zvornik. Those tensions became to -- began to appear, rather, when the national parties came to power and when the influence of nationalism from outside Bosnia and Herzegovina started to be felt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts. Judge Hanoteau read out of paragraph 19, I think he read a single ethnic members family, it appears now as it also appears in the statement as "single ethic members family." From comparing compares with the B/C/S, which reads [B/C/S spoken] I take it that it's a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think that is a typographical error and I think it's clear from the witness's answer that he is referring to ethnic members of the families.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that has been corrected for the sake of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could refer to the next still.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, are any of the faces in this still familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I know the first man we can see on the screen. I don't know his name, but I know that he is from a suburb of Bajer in the city of Zvornik. He's somewhat younger than me so I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Do you know what nationality he is?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: He is Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And that particular still I'm referring to appears at 22 minutes 58 on the tape. So if we could refer to the next still which is 23 minutes 47. Do you recognise any of the faces in this still?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: The person to the right is Muhamed Dzinic who was maybe 200 or 300 meters from the house where I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And what ethnicity is this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've finished with the stills and that video. If I could now present as a bundle, the next four exhibits and that's numbers 12, 13, 14 and 15. I note that the diary which is marked as number 12 already as an exhibit number, P48. If the next three exhibits could be given exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the facsimile from Petar Jankovic which seems to be dated the 23rd of March would receive number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That Your Honours would be Prosecution Exhibit P653. And the translation would be P653.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The next one would be the interview with Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That, Your Honours, would be Prosecution Exhibit P654 and the translation would be P654.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the last one, that is a list of payments to members of the Zvornik TO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That, Your Honours, would be Prosecution Exhibit P655, with the English translation at P655.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, if I could refer to you written document which is a diary of Petar Jankovic, do you know who Petar Jankovic is?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: He was the president of SDS in Kalesija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And Mr. Mehinagic, if I could refer you to an entry for the 24th of January 1992, and you'll note that there is an 8-digit number above the handwritten 24 January 1992, that's 0018-5104, and the next page is 0018-0105. There's a particular passage that I would like to read to you and receive your comment on which appears in the first few paragraphs of that entry, and that is the following, the entry says: "All this time I have been working on securing the weapons and cooperating with the Tuzla corps especially General Jankovic and Colonel Nikola Dendzic [phoen]. I categorise Nikola as a good Serb. He promised to help to get to the weapons and we are working on that. As at the 24th of January 1992, were you aware that General Jankovic and Colonel Nikola were working together with the SDS in Kalesija?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This is the first time I'm seeing this. I'm very surprised that my friend Jankovic as a JNA commander was supplying the SDS with any weapons. And secondly, according to my information, in certain situations, Commander Jankovic was, how should I say that, formally a commander, but Nikola Dendzic ^ called the shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And I'd now like to refer you to a further entry in this diary, and this is an entry for the 17th of January 1992 [sic]. And if you look at those 8 digit numbers again at you could find the 8-digit sequence which is 0018-5117 and the entry continues on through to 0018-5119, and I'd just like to read the following to you. That says here, "That the meeting was attended by commanders Tacic, Lalic, and commanders of troops and platoons. Commanders asked questions about weapons. Tacic tried to avoid answering. He said it should be arranged with Lalic. Lalic is going through the lists and smiling. Then there are the proposals that were set forward by the author Petar Jankovic and that -- they were the following: That Lalic be appointed commander. That a battalion be named Majevicko-Bircanski, the problem of Muslims, the volunteers in Dubrava who are "taking Dubrava from the inside," doesn't develop that any further, and the fourth conclusion is "radio connections issue. I propose that they be uniform." Then it says "Tacic agreed and accepted everything." Eventually it concludes that, "Tacic congratulated me on wise proposals and observations."
