We can see from the evidence that's been admitted in writing that you are familiar with Colonel Radoslav Tacic. Did you know that he was liaising with the Kalesija SDS in the manner described here as at the end of January 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I didn't know, and I was very surprised and disappointed by his disloyal linking up with the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, when you said to the 17th of January in the transcript, I take it that you wanted to refer to the 27th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that was in error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, if you could put the diary to one side now and if you could refer to the document which is a handwritten facsimile and that's a facsimile from Petar Jankovic and it's addressed to the attention of Minister Ostojic. Are you aware as at around about March 1992 who Minister Ostojic was?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a minister in the government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Do you know what his first name is and do you know whether he continued to be a minister in Bosnia and Herzegovina or alternatively with the Serbian government in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: He is a minister in the army of the -- he was a minister in the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina all the way until the war.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In the government, the interpreter's correction, in the government, not the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The facsimile reads that "the Serbian people are grateful for the material and moral support in these difficult times. We saw who is loyal and disloyal. "Political and strategic decisions have been coordinated with the corps command and the 4th armoured brigade. I wish you success in the creation of Serbian state in Bosnia-Herzegovina." First of all, were you aware that as at 23 March 1992, Petar Jankovic was coordinating political and strategic decisions with the corps command and could you just describe to the Court who constituted the corps command in the region?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I did not know and I am very disappointed to find out that the JNA engaged in such cooperation with the SDS because these are unconstitutional activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Secondly, as to your question in relation to this command, corps commander was General Savo Jankovic and the chief of staff of the corps was General Rajko Lapcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I know a couple of other people, in case you are interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: That's sufficient, Mr. Mehinagic. The next reference is to the coordination of political and strategic decisions with the fourth armoured brigade. In your statement, you've referred to Radoslav Tacic's role as the commander of an armoured battalion and you've referred to Dragan Obrenovic's role as the commander of a unit. Are you aware whether -- are you aware as to the command, who were the commanders of the brigade described as the 4th Armoured Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radoslav Tacic was a commander of an armoured mechanised brigade which after the withdrawal from Jasta Barsko [phoen], I can see the date here on the 27th of January so, he apparently he was already there but at any rate in the month of January I knew that they had come to the area of Tuzla and his command post was at Paprace. One battalion was deployed in the area, in the broader area of Dubrava airport and one battalion was deployed in the area of Zvornik and another in the area between Zvornik and Bijeljina, so that was the establishment of that brigade, three battalions and about 100 armoured vehicles. The commander of this armoured and mechanised battalion that was stayed in the area of Zvornik was Captain Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next sentence aid like to write on is "I wish you success in the creation of the Serbian state." That's the concluding sentence in the paragraph referring to the political and strategic decisions being coordinated with the corps command. How do you respond seeing that on a facsimile dated 23 March 1992, that is the sentence, "I wish you success in the creation of a Serbian state in BH"?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: My first impression is that this is profoundly anti- and non-constitutional.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd like to now refer you to the next document - I've finished with that facsimile - and that is a list of payments for the members of the TO of the municipality of Zvornik. Now, just for transcript references, the facsimile was P653 and I'm now referring to P655 which is a list of payments to members of the Zvornik Territorial Defence for April and it records that for April, there are three names who were in combat for 30 days and accordingly are entitled to payment, and the second name on the list there, Dragan Obrenovic. Were you aware that he was part of the Territorial Defence of Zvornik in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I wasn't and all the way until the 8th of April, I was in touch with him, in fact, as a commander of the -- of a JNA battalion. I'm extremely surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, I've finished with that document. If we can refer now to the interview with Dragan Obrenovic which is P654, and there's a section in this interview which commences with the -- wherein he responds to the question, "What task did your unit have upon its arrival in Zvornik?" And that's on page 2 of the English translation, and I think it's also appearing on the second page of the B/C/S which is 01148237. I'll just refer you to specific matters. Can you confirm that following your arrival here in The Hague, you've had an opportunity to read this article?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I was shown the article in the course of my proofing for this testimony. I had never seen or heard of it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now I just refer you to the opening sentence in his answer to that question, "What task did your union have upon its arriving in Zvornik," he says, "The unit that was under my command came to Zvornik in February 1992 from the Dubrava airport near Zuvaniva [phoen]." Were you aware that that was the case?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: There's two things here. First of all, I was the one who, since December of 2001 [as interpreted], kept insisting that the JNA should take over the guarding of these bridges and organise these activities. And, secondly, when Lieutenant Tacic came along with his brigade, General Jankovic sent him to introduce himself to me and establish an official contact, and he brought the captain, Dragan Obrenovic, along and introduced him as a local commander in the area and I came across him on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Then there is a reference to you in the third paragraph, which is the last paragraph in the B/C/S on the left-hand column and it says that he arrived, Obrenovic, at the hotel Jezero. All the elite were there headed by Pasic, Juzbasic, and Izet Mehinagic, it says "Mehinagic pulled many strings behind the scenes, he was quite eloquent and a close friend of the then-Commander of the 17th corps, General Savo Jankovic," and he continues to describe the situation. In your statement at paragraphs 39 to 49, you set out in detail a meeting of the first session of the Council of National Defence. Can you confirm that the reference here by Obrenovic is to that meeting that you refer to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: At this stage, too, I'd just like to move ahead and present to you the document which I think is 18 on the exhibit list. I apologise to my case manager for surprising her with this. That's an excerpt from your diary. Your Honour, if that document could be given a -- an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be given a number once it has been distributed. Meal while, Mr. Margetts, may I ask your attention for P655.1, where the translation seems to be incomplete especially the handwriting below the total 39.500 is missing. But I could imagine that that is the same but then in words rather than in digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will attend to that and complete the translation appropriately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if it's just the same but we could resolve the matter right away. If it could be shown to the interpreters by putting it on the ELMO, then we could perhaps find out whether this is just repetition of the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm informed by the -- my case manager that the interpreters have a copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm talking and I'm now addressing the booth or the several booths, that the list for payments to the members of the TO contains some handwritten text below 93.500. Could one of the booths, preferably the English one inform me about what it says, if it's just the number in words.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can't find the bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It then could be shown on the ELMO for one second. Madam Registrar, if you would focus on the bottom and at the right hand. I still don't see the ELMO picture on my screen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: You mean the text right beneath 93.500.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in brackets there is a few words which do not appear in the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That is just the sum of 93.500 in letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I thought it would be but -- so let's proceed. There's no need to provide another translation. Ms. Loukas, I take it that with this explanation -- Ms. Loukas, I take it that with this explanation that you will be satisfied that what appears between brackets is just in words the same as the number of --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, Your Honour, my case manager has just been confirming that to me as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let's just proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then the exhibit number to be assigned to the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next Prosecution Exhibit, Your Honours, would be P656 and the English translation would be P656.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, could you please refer you to the document before you and confirm that that's a copy of an extract from your diary that you maintained in April 1992, an extract of your entry for the 6th of April, 1992, and I'm referring to Exhibit P656.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have the original of the diary with me for inspection by the Defence or by the Bench if you would like to inspect it. Mr. Mehinagic wishes to maintain this as a historical record for himself, but it is available for inspection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm happy to inspect it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we could continue at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please -- and I'd like to have a look at it as well. Give it to Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the next two exhibits could be presented to the witness, that's numbers 16 and 17 in the exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The diary is just for -- the only question was identification, that this is the diary of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the numbers please. I take it you'd prefer to have number 16 on your list first, Mr. Margetts, that would be order dated --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: 5 April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 5 April 1992. Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next Prosecution Exhibit number for the order issued on the 5th of April, 1992 would be P657.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next, the list of 120-millimetre battery personnel would be Prosecution Exhibit P658.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, in your statement at paragraph 30 you refer to the fact that you obtained information that the mobilisation of the Serbian Territorial Defence had been ordered on the 4th of April, 1992. I'd like to look at the document which is P657 and is a decision of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality dated 5 April 1992 and a signature appears at the bottom of that document. First of all, can you confirm that that is the signature of Mr. Brano Grujic as it is depicted on this document?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I cannot confirm anybody's signatures but the contents do correspond to the events at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehinagic. If I could refer you to the next document and that is P658 and that's a list of a 120-millimetre battery crew I refer you to the note at the bottom that the battery crew was active with the JNA from the 4th of April 1992 and it's signed by Dragan Gotovac. First of all, do you know who Dragan Gotovac is?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Dragan Gotovac has a degree in law. He is currently a lawyer in Zvornik and before the war, he was the president of the municipal branch of the youth organisation. I know him very well. We are not friends really, but he is much younger than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Referring to this document, and the reference to a 120-millimetre battery crew and it being active with the JNA from 4 April 1992, do you have any information in relation to the activities of this battery crew in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I was very surprised by the fact that Dragan Gotovac was in this formation and that this formation had at all been established prior to the attack on Zvornik. During the attack on Zvornik, since I had -- I was the one who knew most about the military matters as a civilian, I knew a lot about the weapons employed. And the weapons included the ones mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: On the 8th of April when you observed the mortar fire on Zvornik, were you able to determine from what type of -- or what type of mortar was being fired?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to observe that. As far as the anti-aircraft weapons are concerned, I had done the training for squad leader and I was therefore able to clearly see that 57/2 millimetre anti-aircraft pieces were employed. In this interview, Dragan Obrenovic does confirm that such weapons were deployed around Zvornik. I could distinguish also the fire of the -- the fire from 120-millimetre artillery pieces and 82 millimetre pieces. At that point I had the assistant commander of the municipal TO staff of Zvornik with me, Pandur who was also familiar with different weaponry from the experience he had from military drills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You said you could distinguish the fire from a -- 120-millimetre artillery pieces. When you say that do you mean you could observe it at the time?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've finished with that document. If I could now present the next three documents, they are the ones that are numbered 20 to 22 in the listing. If they could be assigned exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you assign numbers to them and at the same time, could I ask whether Ms. Loukas is ready with inspecting the original of the diary? Ms. Loukas, if you put on your headphones then there's a fair chance that you also hear --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's okay, Your Honour, I was reading your observations on the computer. Your Honour, Mr. Krajisnik wanted to have a look at the diary and I was just going to ensure that he had an opportunity to look at it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And once Mr. Krajisnik is finished with it, we'd like to have a look at it. Please proceed. Mr. Registrar, the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, number 20, the order of General, dated the 10th of April 1992, would be given Prosecution Exhibit P659. Number 21 which is the daily operational report dated 13th April 1992 would be given Prosecution Exhibit P660. And the third one which is number 22, the daily combat report dated the 18th April, 1992 would be given Prosecution Exhibit P661.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, if I could refer first to the document that's been given the number P659, and that's the order of General Savo Jankovic of the 10th of April, 1992, and this a request to carry out combat action on the 11th of April with fighter bombers aiming at Kula in Zvornik and this is to neutralise forces attacking our units. Reading that order, are you familiar with the activities that were taking place in Kula and do you know which forces Jankovic intended to attack with his fighter bombers?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Based on all the information I received and based on the evidence that could be found at Kula later on, there were no weapons there that would be capable of targeting bridges. This order here explains and talks about the activity of fighter bombers that I was able to see as they were firing upon Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: So Savo Jankovic has ordered an attack on Kula. What forces was he attacking with fighter bombers?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of April, 1992, there could only have been defence forces of Zvornik and civilians at Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next document I'd like -- I've finished with that document if we could refer to the next document, P660 which is 13 April 1992, Mr. Mehinagic, if I could refer you to the signature on this 13 April 1992 daily operative report, and that's the signature of Colonel Bozo Milohanovic, can you confirm that that's the same gentleman that participated in the radio interview that we saw earlier today with you in Tuzla on the 9th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, Colonel Bozo Milohanovic was assistant commander for morale, assistant commander of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could refer you to the item 7 which is the security situation in the territory, it talks about a bus of green berets leaving the SDA headquarters in Tuzla and it says that there should be 6.000 of them gathered. Can you comment on the presence of green berets at Tuzla and the number quoted by Colonel Milohanovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of the presence of any green berets at Tuzla and in this period, on the 13th of April, Tuzla had organised columns of vehicles to meet the thousands of refugees fleeing Zvornik so that they would not be forced to walk 50 kilometres. I'm convinced that the number of 60.000 is the result of the propaganda that was promoted by its authors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'm finished with that document. If we could move to P661 and I could refer you to the last paragraph before item 4, and that appears in the middle of page 2 of the English translation, and it appears at the bottom, I believe, or actually it appears at the top of page 2 of the Bosnian translation, this is a top secret daily combat report of 18 April 1992 signed by Savo Jankovic. Mr. Mehinagic, in that portion I've referred to, Jankovic states, "In the course of the day, the 336th Motorised Brigade with the units of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik Territorial Defence were engaged in combat activities," and it states "against paramilitary formations, green berets in the Kula grad area." When you see this signed by Savo Jankovic, were you aware at that time of 18 April 1992, that the JNA 336th Motorised Brigades was engaged in combat activities with the units of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Officially, of course, I was not familiar with this, but this official report confirms that the JNA did attack Kula and the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Do you have any comment to make in respect of the fact that this JNA unit is referred to as being engaged in combat operations with the Zvornik TO?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This was a treacherous relationship because the commander, Colonel Tacic, publicly announced to the people in Zvornik that the JNA was going to defend the town in case it came under attack whilst he was, in fact, on the side of the attackers. I feel pity for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic -- or in fact, I'll address you in a moment, Mr. Mehinagic. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could present to the witness the next series of documents, that's documents 23, 24, 25, and 27 on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If they could be assigned exhibit numbers, noting that number 25 already has an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number 23 which is the conclusion on the appointment of the commission for negotiations, dated 20th April 1992, will be given the next Prosecution Exhibit Number P662. Number 24 which is the decision on formation of the municipality of Zvornik in exile, dated 8 May 1992, will be given Prosecution Exhibit P663. Number 26 which is the order --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, number 26 will not be presented, that's a duplication of an earlier exhibit that we had, number 6, I think, so the next one is number 27.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number 27 which is the decision on the formation of war staff and war secretariat dated 20th May 1992 would be given Prosecution Exhibit Number P664.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, I refer you first of all to a document dated 20 April 1992 and headed "Conclusion on Appointment of the Commission for Negotiations," and I note that the members of that commission include, at number 2, somebody referred to as Ljubisa Mauzer, do you have any information about someone referred to as Ljubisa Mauzer?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I'm very much surprised to see his name in this context because Ljubisa Mauzer was not a resident of the Zvornik municipality at the time at all. I know that later on, he played an important role in the exchanges organised during the war. He was a prominent commander of one of the units of Republika Srpska. After the war, he held a high position in the police of Republika Srpska. Several years ago, he was killed in an assassination carried out in Bijeljina in bright daylight. That's why I actually know him as a man from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, I'd now like to refer you to the next document which is a proclamation to the population of Zvornik municipality which is a document referred to in your witness statement and it's referred to at paragraphs 80 through to 84 of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd just like to read into the record or -- although Your Honour, I note the time and I don't have a lot to go through but I think it will take me at least 15 minutes to do so. So I would like to proceed. But how I proceed will depend on whether or not I could seek the indulgence of the Court to take a little bit of the third session today. I apologise for that, given that the earlier indication was we wouldn't go into the third session but some technical difficulties and other matters have been unexpected and caused this slight delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's say this is an explanation in part. You've got another 15 minutes after the break, that means that we'll have a break until quarter to 1.00. You'll then have until 1.00 to -- 15 minutes, you said, would approximately do. We start at exactly quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just before Mr. Margetts proceeds, Your Honour, I just want to foreshadow that there's a matter on the LiveNote that I want to deal with at some point. But I realise that Mr. Margetts has limited time but I just want to foreshadow I'd like to raise it at a later point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, just before the break, one -- I have made an application for slightly more time, and so our time is very restricted, so I need to take you through these documents very quickly. But the document before you which is a proclamation to the population of Zvornik municipality, is that the document that you faxed to the TO, Territorial Defence of Zvornik, and to Radio Zvornik which is referred to in your witness statement and it's at paragraphs 80 to 84?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. And the reference there is to Exhibit P663. I'd now like to turn to the two decisions which are Exhibit P529 and Exhibit P664, the first one is dated 28 April and the second one is dated the 20th of May. Mr. Mehinagic, turning first to the one dated 28 April, which is P529 and is the "Decision on Forming the TO Command of the Municipality of Zvornik," do you recognise the name Marko Pavlovic as the TO staff commander as being the same person that you referred to in those paragraphs 80 to 84 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And again in respect of the next document, Mr. Mehinagic, if I can take your attention to the document 20th of May, 1992, which is P664 and it's headed "Decision on Reorganisation and Creation of Organs of the Provisional Government, the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik." Two names appear in Article 4 and they are the names Marko Pavlovic and Dragan Obrenovic. Are they the people that we have referred to earlier in the evidence that's been presented to the Court today?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, that moves me to the next series of documents. I've finished with those documents, and I'd like to present the series of documents and have exhibit numbers for 28 through 32 noting that the document 31 is already assigned a number P583. Secondly, there is a press article which is not listed on the exhibit list but I have -- we provided a translation earlier to the Defence and I've now provided the Bosnian copy of the press article and the translation to the Defence. I'd like to add that document and for description purposes, I guess if we could add the number 36 to the potential exhibit list and it could record the ERN numbers for the original. 0149760, and for the translation, ET B014-9758, B014-9760. Of course if that document could be given an exhibit number as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please assign numbers, I think we start with the statement the 31st of May, 1992 of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be, Your Honours, Prosecution Exhibit number P665. The next one which is number 29, "report on crimes committed in Zvornik municipality" dated the 16th June 1992 would be Prosecution Exhibit P666. The next number which is number 30, the "report on crimes committed dated 17 June 1992" would be Prosecution Exhibit P667. Number 32 which is the order dated 31st May, 1992 would be given Prosecution Exhibit P668.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if also the one I've just added which I added as number 36 which had the -- sorry, as number 36 -- I apologise again, I seem to have a different listing than my case manager and she has pointed out to me that my references to 36 are in error and I should be referring to an additional document, number 35, and that description we gave earlier which was of the original ERN B014-9760, if that could be referring to an additional document number 35 and that description we gave earlier which was of the original ERN B014-9760, if that could be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number 35 would be given Prosecution Exhibit number P669.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, in your statement, you refer to the fact that when you left Zvornik, you formed what was to become an association for refugees, you also established the municipal commission for the investigation of war crimes, and you also formed the Zvornik municipality in exile. And you detail in your statement the fact that refugees came to Tuzla and you received information from them. Now, due to a lack of time I'm not able to go into the substance of the various documents that are before us but if we can just take them in turn, if you could first refer to the statement of 31st May, 1992 that's before you and can you confirm that that accurately sets out information you received from refugees that came from Zvornik, and that's Exhibit P665.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I confirm that it's my statement. It is about one of the first statements taken after the Municipal Committee for the Investigation of War Crimes was set up in the process of reestablishing the municipal authorities and the functioning of the authorities in the municipality of Tuzla. So this is the result of everything I'd heard from the refugees, the civil defence, the members of the Presidency, and others that we managed to hear from and we had meetings on a daily basis and assessed the situation on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next document I'd like to refer to is the press article which is dated 9 June 1992 from the paper the Crni List and you can see that there is a reference there to similar material to the material in the statement, does that set out information you received from the refugees? That's Exhibit P669.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This article is the result of an official press conference that, on behalf of the municipality of Zvornik, I organised on the 8th of June, 1992, and that was two months after the attack on Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And I'll compress the next two documents that are similar in nature. The one that is assigned the exhibit number P666 is dated 16 June 1992 and is addressed to the Presidency of BiH and other recipients and the one that is P667 is dated 17 June 1992, appears to be a description of information you've received in an appeal for help to the Presidency of the republic of BiH. Again, can you confirm that the information set out in these documents is information you received from refugees?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the refugees and the official authorities of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, there are two orders, if we could put those documents aside, there are two orders, there's one dated the 28th of May, 1992 and there's one dated the 31st of May 1992. Let's take the first one in date order, and that's the exhibit P583. Both of these documents are signed off by Svetozar Andric. Did you know of Svetozar Andric, and I don't need you to go into detail of how you met him, but if you could inform the Court as to whether you obtained any information about his role in around the middle of 1992.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I met him from the Territorial Defence Staff for the municipality in Tuzla in conjunction with my duties in this respect. I saw him in the beginning of the war when Republika Srpska units were still being set up and it was a very unpleasant surprise to me, because I had known him quite well beforehand. And afterwards I got information from the media or in other ways relating to his activities until this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd like to refer you to paragraph 6, and paragraph 6 states as follows, and it says, "The moving out of the Muslim population must be organised and coordinated with the municipalities through which the moving is carried out. Only women and children can move out while men fir for military service are to be placed in camps for exchange." In terms of your role in receiving refugees in Tuzla, is that consistent with your observations as to who moved out and who remained in camps?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: This order simply completes the picture as to why all this had happened and why men were left behind and why there were killings afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next order which is Exhibit P668 is again reportedly signed by Mr. Andric. It's dated the 31st of May, 1992. In the preamble it refers to a "decision of the Birac Serb autonomous region government which regulates the moving out of the Muslim population from the territory of Birac." The refugees you received in Tuzla, were they from the region of Birac?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: The region of Birac encompassed part of the municipality of Zvornik as well so it referred to the Zvornik area as well, even though until today I've never seen any documents coming from the government of that so-called region and I don't really know what people were in this so-called government. I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In regard to that, you did see a television programme, I think. Earlier in your evidence, you mentioned where a gentleman by the name of Milic was appointed to a regional authority; if you could confirm with us that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: I said that I saw the founding Assembly for that region but afterwards, I saw nothing else emanating from that region or any person carrying out any duties, and Mr. Milic was not a dignitary of the region, he was a just a member, a participant in that Assembly, and he was sitting in the first row.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehinagic. I've finished with those documents. If I could now provide to the witness the documents that appear as 33 and 34 on the list, that is a transcript of an interview and I'd like to show that interview of Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic and I'd also like the witness to receive the document which is the data on various objects in the region. If those documents could be assigned exhibit numbers. In regard to the video, we will provide a CD of the video and if we could -- if number 35 could be numbered first and the video numbered second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar. I think 35, you're suffering from the same problem you were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm suffering from the same problem I was five minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that. So you'd first have the data on Vakuf objects in the region of Doboj to be numbered first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would then be, Mr. Registrar ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be, Your Honours, P670.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the interview with Krajisnik and Karadzic between January and March 1993 would be P671.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, do you have before you a document listing various mosques?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the mosques described therein, that you observed them prior to April 1992 in the localities that are described in this list?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: Since I was working at the municipal level for a long time, I did visit all those places and so I do know of their existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Subsequent to the dates that are listed in this table, did you either observe that these mosques were destroyed or alternatively, were you informed by others that these mosques were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: After I was told and after the war, I visited all those places and I realised and saw for myself that the mosques had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Mehinagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'd now like to play a short excerpt of a video to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I then take it that, looking at the clock, Mr. Margetts you used your 15 minutes so let's just do the sequence, and then I may take it that you are finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I just have some questions on the sequence that I'd like to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, try to limit them to the core questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinagic, if you could just view this video that's going to be presented on the screen, it's an interview with Karadzic and Krajisnik conducted by Mr. Risto Djogo which was shown sometime between January and March of 1993. We just have a short excerpt to orient the Court and the witness to the transcript, it is -- the translators as well if you could look to the reference 02:38:04 which is page 29 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, technical difficulties once again have arisen with the playing of this video so we won't be playing the video at this time. But what I will do is I will just refer Mr. Mehinagic to the transcript that I just referred to, and I'm referring to the portion between 02:38:04 and 02:39:07. Mr. Krajisnik is asked by Mr. Djogo in early 1993, "What will happen to Zvornik, one of the many disputed towns and areas according to the Vance-Owen plan?" Mr. Krajisnik says, "We'll have to be realistic about Zvornik because it's now inhabited by our refugees from Zenica and other towns where ethnical cleansing was committed against Serbs." Mr. Krajisnik then proceeds, and he says, "Once Serbs return to Zenica, Muslims will return to Zvornik, Vance and Owen will have to understand that there is a natural migration of people that Serbs fled Zenica and Muslims fled Tuzla and Zenica." Mr. Mehinagic, from your observation was the migration of people natural?

utterances.speaker: IZET MEHINAGIC
utterances.text: There was enforced ethnic cleansing whereby Muslims had to leave Zvornik and I can't say anything about Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In your statement which has been admitted into evidence, you refer to the negotiations that took place and the situation in regard to the proposed agreement for division of the Zvornik municipality. Mr. Krajisnik says in this interview that -- the following: "We think that the division of the Zvornik municipality should have been accepted, as was proposed before the war." You've indicated to the Court what your view of the division of the proposed division of the municipality was, what's your view of Mr. Krajisnik's comments? Well, to put it another way, was the proposed division before the war an acceptable proposal?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this question has already been asked of the witness and there seems to be little point to proceeding with this question. It's just gilding the lily as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Margetts. It seems to use now the system to put a marker somewhere by putting a question two times. Mr. Margetts, the question has been asked, the question has been answered. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I believe similarly, the matters that are referred to in the rest of the quotation of Mr. Krajisnik has also been addressed during the course of the evidence, and I draw Your Honours' attention, and that concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Margetts. Ms. Loukas. Are you ready to cross-examine the witness? We would start tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, situation is that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a matter to be raised in the presence of the witness or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, there's no need for the presence of the witness.

utterances.text: Then we'll inform Mr. Mehinagic that -- Mr. Mehinagic, it has been arranged that your examination and

utterances.text: we might have gone on for half an hour, not more, but it's more practical to start tomorrow morning. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Just very briefly, this is a reference to the bottom of page 46, beginning of page 47, bottom of page 46, beginning of page 47 of the LiveNote today. Mr. Margetts referred the witness to a particular document. He asked him about -- Your Honours will note there the question is asked, "Do you know who Petar Jankovic is?" The witness is -- answer is he was the president of the SDS in Kalesija. The next question recites a passage from the document, and then Mr. Margetts asks this question, "As of the 24th of January 1992, were you aware that Jankovic and Nikola were working together with the SDS in Kalesija?" Now, Your Honour, I've examined the portions of the document that have been tendered in evidence to see if that particular nexus could be made. Now, Your Honours, on the whole of the evidence, it may be that Your Honours may or may not take the inference that there was that involvement, but to put that in the question on the basis of the document is, in fact, not correct, because if a person is a functionary of a particular party and there's something in his diary that may or may not lead the court to the inference that there was involvement of the two institutions that are talked about in the question, but to actually put the evidence in the question, as it were, is, Your Honour, in my view, thoroughly objectionable. I took the time to actually go through the portions that Mr. Margetts has put into evidence just so that I wouldn't have a knee-jerk reaction in relation to this, in case unless there was something in the document that might have taken the matter further. But Your Honour, there isn't and I do place an objection to that sort of question. At this point, I guess, it's really basically a marker, but one really shouldn't -- the evidence shouldn't come from the mouth of the Prosecutor, it -- it's quite clear there what the document says and that the inference thereafter is a matter for the Trial Chamber and not a matter to be placed in that leading form on the basis of that document before the witness and that's the matter I put there now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, any need to respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's our position that the document itself and the evidence adduced from the witness relating to the author of the document does, as Ms. Loukas states, leave that inference open to the Trial Chamber and that inference remains open to the Trial Chamber and I don't see Ms. Loukas objecting to that inference being a possible inference, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, that's not what she's doing. I think you might not have fully understood what Ms. Loukas is saying. Ms. Loukas says that if you ask the witness about the awareness of working together immediately following questions about certain documents, that you could only do that if it would be beyond any dispute that from those documents it appears that they were working together, and not to put such a conclusion to the witness, of course hoping that it would confirm that where there's no other basis than the documents, because the witness clearly testified here that he for the first time saw these -- well, that's in his answer that he for the first time saw it. Do you understand, first of all, what the objection was, and also that your response was not fully addressing the matter raised by Ms. Loukas?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do understand. I'm now in a position to respond more directly to the issue. The fact is it seems to be an objection to a leading question and the assumptions of evidence in that question, Ms. Loukas is saying, don't exist either in the document or the transcript. It's our position that those -- the assumed facts do exist in the document and in the transcript. If an analysis of the document further -- a reference to -- it has a reference to Mr. Ostojic, a member of the SDS -- sorry, Your Honour I'm moving to another document. So the submission is yes, that we say that the assumed facts existed in evidence and the question is not a leading question insofar as the record already reflected those matters and the question was merely building on that record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you're just asking the witness to draw a conclusion from that evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: What we were asking the question -- what we were asking the witness to do was given the evidence that was on the record from his answers to the previous question, and the document, to tell us whether or not he was aware of the connections that were evident from that evidence in any express, direct way. I think his answer was that he wasn't aware and that has relevance for various reasons and that was the further information we sought from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not spend too much time on it. Ms. Loukas blames you for asking for an awareness of a fact which, in her view, has not been established until that moment, that makes the question a leading one because if the question suggests a fact to exist which has not been established that's one of the varieties of leading questions. You say it did exist. And then you say also it's relevant to establish whether he was aware of it or not. I do not exactly see yet what the relevance of that is, because from his statement, it may be clear that he was not aware of any such working together. That also means that that at least was a fact which was in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
